title: Equinoxe Infinity
label: Columbia Records
overview: Released 16 November 2018 on Columbia Records, Jarre's 20th studio album arrives exactly forty years after Equinoxe (1978), using Yamaha CS-80, ARP 2600, EMS VCS 3, EMS Synthi AKS, Eminent 310 Unique, Mellotron, Korg MS-20, Moog Sub 37, Moog Taurus 1, Erica Synths Modular, and a prototype GR-1 granular synthesizer (Tasty Chips Electronics) alongside Arturia virtual instruments and Spectrasonics Omnisphere. Ten movements form a continuous arc from sparse atmospheric prelude through mechanical intensity to a seven-minute finale; Movement 5 is intentionally brief — a structural callback to 'Band In The Rain' (Equinoxe Part 8, 1978), processed using the GR-1 on a child's voice recording. Recorded at JMJ Studio, Paris; cover artwork by Filip Hodas in two variants — a hopeful ecological image and a dystopian alternate — both reworking Michel Granger's original Le trac composition. Charts: Germany #11, France #20, UK #33.

tracks.title: The Watchers (Movement 1)
tracks.role: Album role: The album's sentinel opening — a sparse atmospherics-first movement that establishes the Equinoxe timbral vocabulary before any directed motion begins. At under three minutes it functions as a prelude, placing the listener inside the sound world rather than beginning a narrative.

events.description: near-inaudible low-frequency texture, no percussive element. Pure harmonic space.
events.detail: The CS-80's slow-attack polyphonic pads set the Equinoxe register immediately — the same timbral DNA as the 1978 original, warmly layered.

events.description: characteristic pitch-gliding single-voice line over sustained harmony; slow, searching.
events.detail: The Yamaha CS-80 is the album's defining instrument, used throughout. Its portamento mode allows pitch to slide between notes in a way no digital synthesizer replicates accurately.

events.description: not yet a rhythm section — an underlying low-frequency motion that implies pulse without asserting it.
events.detail: The Moog Taurus pedal tones appear here: sub-bass motion that is felt rather than analytically heard. The bass register opens the dynamic range for what follows.

events.description: the opening melody completes its single phrase; the movement releases into the space leading to Movement 2.
events.detail: Movement 1 asks no questions and answers none. Its function is orientation. It is the period of silence before a concert begins.

tracks.title: Flying Totems (Movement 2)
tracks.role: Album role: The album's first full movement — the energy establishes a sequenced melodic line and a sense of directed forward motion. Contrasts the prelude's stasis with purposeful arrival.

events.description: immediate rhythmic character from the first note; the movement begins without atmospheric preamble.
events.detail: The ARP 2600's semi-modular architecture gives it characteristic tonal variation between repeated notes — each arpeggio step has a slightly different timbral colour.

events.description: a second voice — polyphonic, slower, providing harmonic support above the sequenced pulse.
rhythm emerges: not hard-edged, soft and supportive. The album's first explicit rhythmic framework.
events.detail: The Minipops rhythm unit provides a pattern consistent with the Equinoxe archetype; percussive but never dominating the tonal content.

events.description: sequence and melody at maximum combined density. The movement's structural apex.
events.detail: At 3:54 this is one of the album's shorter full movements; its economy is a structural virtue — it does exactly what it needs to do before exiting.

events.description: elements exit one by one; the movement resolves cleanly without a hard cut.

tracks.title: Robots Don't Cry (Movement 3)
tracks.role: Album role: The album's longest movement and its greatest intensity — a five-minute build that concentrates the sequential arc's forward energy into its most fully orchestrated and rhythmically dense single piece. The title is the album's most explicit conceptual statement about automation.

events.description: immediate rhythmic urgency, more mechanical in character than Movement 2; the tempo intention is clear from the first beat.
events.detail: The ARP 2600's hard-sync pulsing and the Erica Synths modular system's clock-driven sequences establish a mechanistic grid that makes the title's subject matter audible.

events.description: a second sequence introduced over the first, creating rhythmic and harmonic counterpoint.
events.detail: Jarre's counterpoint approach is characteristically pre-digital: two sequences running in parallel at different rates, the interference pattern between them creating the melodic interest.

events.description: percussion arrives at full weight; CS-80 pads sustain beneath the sequences; the arrangement reaches its widest dynamic band.
events.detail: This is the most densely produced point in the album's first half. The contrast between this moment and Movement 1's near-silence underlines the arc being constructed.

events.description: most layers suspended; the underlying clock-pulse left exposed briefly before reconstruction.
events.detail: The structural pause makes the re-entry of the full arrangement feel like a gain in force rather than a repetition.

events.description: all elements return simultaneously; the movement's highest dynamic point.
the mechanical energy drains systematically; the movement empties before Movement 4.

tracks.title: All That You Leave Behind (Movement 4)
tracks.role: Album role: Emotional mid-point and tonal pivot — after Movement 3's mechanistic intensity, a spacious, expressive piece that restores the album's introspective register. The Mellotron's presence situates the emotional territory squarely in the 1978 Equinoxe lineage.

events.description: the immediately warmer timbral quality signals the movement's different emotional register.
events.detail: The Mellotron, present on both the 1978 Equinoxe and this sequel, is the album's most obviously nostalgic instrument choice. Its tape-replay characteristic warmth is specific and irreproducible.

events.description: a broad, expressive melody on the CS-80; slower note values and wider intervals than the preceding movements.
the chord sequence underneath the melody begins to move; emotional complexity deepens.
Mellotron, CS-80 melody, ARP sequence and rhythm section reach maximum concurrent density.
events.detail: This is the album's most emotionally legible moment: the combination of warm analogue textures, slow melodic movement and the Mellotron's almost-orchestral register.

events.description: the warm textures partially remove themselves; the movement exits with less than it entered with, preparing the listener for the structural surprise of Movement 5.

tracks.title: If the Wind Could Speak (Movement 5)
tracks.role: Album role: The album's structural pivot and its most unusual sound design moment — at 1:32 it is deliberately brief, a structural allusion to 'Band In The Rain' (Equinoxe Part 8, 1978). The GR-1 granular synthesizer, a Kickstarter prototype from Tasty Chips Electronics, processes a recorded child's voice into the texture.

events.section: Immediate minimal texture — GR-1 granular processing
events.description: no introduction: the movement opens with the processed child's voice material, stretched and granularised by the GR-1.
events.detail: The GR-1 granular synthesizer (Tasty Chips Electronics) was not yet commercially available at time of recording; Jarre received a prototype through Kickstarter. Granular synthesis divides audio into small fragments ('grains') and restructures them — the child's voice becomes something between a texture and a melody.

events.description: the granular material moves through the stereo field with a drift suggesting air rather than signal.
events.detail: The movement's title is its structural description: the sound is asked to do what wind does — carry meaning without words. The connection to Equinoxe 1978 Part 8 is intentional and acknowledged by Jarre.

events.description: the granular texture sustains briefly, then releases completely. The movement's ending is its most quiet point.
events.detail: The deliberate structural poverty of Movement 5 — under a minute and a half — forces the weight of the album's emotional arc onto the movements that surround it.

tracks.title: Infinity (Movement 6)
tracks.role: Album role: The album's conceptual title piece — the term 'Infinity' is embedded in the album title and these four minutes are its fullest compositional articulation. The movement's harmonic language is the album's most developed: multiple voices, tonal movement, resolution deferred and then delivered.

events.description: the re-establishment of motion after the pivot; the album's energy reasserts itself.
events.detail: After Movement 5's structural compression, this emergence feels earned. The dynamics here are at their most considered in terms of the album's macro-arc.

events.description: the movement's principal voice: a polyphonic melody with harmonic weight absent from the earlier single-note sequences.
events.detail: The CS-80's polyphony is used here deliberately: multiple simultaneous pitches on a single instrument, the chord-melody merge characteristic of Jarre at his most texturally rich.

events.description: the ARP 2600's sequenced patterns return under the CS-80 melody, restoring directed kinetic energy.
the chord sequence moves through its widest range on the album; tonal movement covers the most harmonic ground of any single movement.
events.detail: This is the 'Infinity' of the title as compositional method: harmonic motion that does not repeat the same path.

events.description: the extended harmonic journey completes; the movement exits with clarity into Movement 7.

tracks.title: Machines are Learning (Movement 7)
tracks.role: Album role: The album's most technologically explicit title, concentrated into its second-shortest form. At 2:07 it functions as a compressed statement rather than a development: a pointed comment on automation, delivered briskly.

events.description: a machine-like rhythmic precision from the opening note; the fastest internal pulse of any movement on the album.
events.detail: The 'Machines are Learning' title receives its literal translation: a sequence that repeats with mechanical exactness, the character of a learning algorithm applied to musical structure.

events.description: pads and a melody line respond to the mechanical substrate; human expressiveness over algorithmic precision.
no breakdown, no development; the machine element maintains complete rhythmic continuity to the final note.
events.detail: The lack of a structural breakdown in so short a piece is a formal choice: the machine does not pause, does not breathe.

events.description: the movement ends without a fade; truncated rather than dissolved, entering Movement 8's space cleanly.

tracks.title: The Opening (Movement 8)
tracks.role: Album role: Structurally ironic — named 'The Opening' but placed eighth of ten, functioning as a dramatic re-entry and pre-finale intensification. Re-energises the album from Movement 7's brevity toward the concluding two movements.

events.description: no atmospheric preamble; the movement arrives with all its layers already deployed.
events.detail: The structural surprise: an 'Opening' that opens nothing except the final chapter of the album. The title is the movement's commentary on itself — eighth of ten, but acting as though the finale has just begun.

events.description: sustained portamento melody over a fully deployed rhythm section; the CS-80's long sustain gives the melody a legato quality unlike the earlier percussive sequences.
the tonal centre shifts, adding urgency; the movement is building toward something larger than itself.
events.detail: The modulation is the structural hinge into Movement 9. This movement is consciously transitional — its energy is directed forward.

events.description: the movement reaches its highest intensity before drawing back slightly for the exit.
events.detail: The partial resolution rather than full close keeps tension available for Movement 9. The finale sequence is deliberate and two-stage.

events.description: the layers reduce and the movement transitions seamlessly into the penultimate piece.

tracks.title: Don't Look Back (Movement 9)
tracks.role: Album role: Penultimate movement — its title balances the nostalgic framing of a forty-year sequel against a forward compositional imperative. Each element builds tension available for the finale's full release.

events.section: Driving sequence — no resolution from Movement 8
events.description: immediately continues the energy built in Movement 8; the transition is near-seamless.
events.detail: The album's instruction to itself: do not look back at the 1978 original — or the preceding eight movements — but forward into the finale.

events.description: a melody that, by this stage of the album, reads as a reprise of earlier material rather than an introduction.
the rhythm section reduces; the movement creates space by withdrawing, preparing the finale's maximum dynamic contrast.
events.detail: The withdrawal before the finale is a structural device: the dynamic contrast between the reduced Movement 9 close and Movement 10's full deployment.

events.section: Final build to edge of Movement 10
events.description: the sequence re-energises; total duration of the movement's build is concentrated into the final thirty seconds.
events.detail: Movement 9 hands its unresolved momentum forward without releasing it. The finale inherits maximum available energy.

tracks.title: Equinoxe Infinity (Movement 10)
tracks.role: Album role: All-encompassing finale — at 7:33 the album's longest movement and its fullest emotional deployment. The title restates the album title, situating this piece as the work's defining statement. Builds from the inherited energy of Movement 9 to the album's maximum dynamic range before a spacious, unhurried resolution.

events.section: Full arrangement opens at maximum density
events.description: all instrumental layers deployed from the first bar. No build required: the preceding nine movements have performed the construction.
events.detail: The structural logic of the album pays off here: the first nine movements are preamble. This finale is not an arrival — it is the destination.

events.section: CS-80 principal melody — the title theme
events.description: the album's fullest melodic statement, using the CS-80's polyphony and sustain at their most expressive.
events.detail: On the CS-80, the polyphonic aftertouch — pressure applied to keys after initial contact — controls modulation and expression in real time. What sounds like an orchestral melody is a single player making real-time expressive decisions.

events.description: the chord sequence underneath the principal melody starts its widest movement; the tonal arc of the finale covers the most harmonic ground on the album.
events.detail: This harmonic arc is the payoff for the preceding harmonic restraint of the earlier movements. The finale is harmonically ambitious precisely because the foundations have been carefully laid.

events.description: all elements at maximum combined dynamic; the album's highest point of intensity.
events.detail: Every instrument used across the album is present here simultaneously. The ARP sequences, CS-80 melodies, Mellotron swells, Erica Synths modular textures, and rhythm section at their combined maximum.

events.description: the finale begins its deliberate, unhurried emotional withdrawal; elements exit one by one over two minutes.
events.detail: The coda of the finale is proportionally long by electronic album standards. Jarre gives the resolution as much space as it requires — there is no abrupt ending.

events.description: the last elements — CS-80 pads and sustained chord — release into silence.
events.detail: The album closes as it opened, with a near-inaudible sustained pad texture fading to silence. The circle is closed: the ten movements form a single breath, inhaled and exhaled.
